## The addition, in §1 after the Longo target and before the scope statement

**A counter-anchor.** §1 currently cites only the claim being tested. It should also cite the
published null that predates it.

**Verified by me directly from the source abstract**, `https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.3247`:

> Kate Land, Anže Slosar, Chris Lintott, Dan Andreescu, Steven Bamford, Phil Murray, Robert Nichol,
> M. Jordan Raddick, Kevin Schawinski, Alex Szalay, Daniel Thomas, Jan Vandenberg, **"Galaxy Zoo: The
> large-scale spin statistics of spiral galaxies in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey"**, 2008,
> arXiv:0803.3247. ~37,000 SDSS spirals. The abstract states the winding sense is **"consistent with
> statistical isotropy"**, with **"no significant dipole signal, and thus no evidence for overall
> preferred handedness"**, and — after establishing and correcting for a level of bias — that previous
> studies **"may also be affected and explained by a bias effect."**

**Record that this null predates Longo (2011) and is on a comparable sample.** A preregistration
testing a contested claim must record that the contest has a null on the other side.

## Second: the bias magnitude, as motivation for BS-3's antisymmetry receipt

**The uncorrected Galaxy Zoo 1 handedness asymmetry was ~15%**, attributed to human perception or the
user interface rather than to sky. **The amplitude this study tests is 4%.**

**State that plainly**: an unmeasured classification bias in the same survey family, on the same task,
was nearly four times the signal being sought. That is the motivation for BS-3's
`antisymmetry_receipt` field, and it converts the mirror test from a refinement into a prerequisite.

## Provenance discipline — mark what is second-hand

**I verified the Land abstract directly. I did NOT verify the per-class percentages from Land's own
text** — the primary PDF would not parse, and those numbers reach us through a later reanalysis. So:

- the **null result and the quoted abstract phrases** may be stated as verified from source;
- the **~15% figure and any per-class percentages** must be attributed as **reported by a later
  reanalysis, not read from Land's body text**, or omitted.

**Do NOT cite the mirrored-subset size.** Sources give ~11,000 in one place and 91,303 in another and
I have not resolved which is which. **An unresolved number must not enter the document.**

## Third: the literature is split, and saying so is honest

A later reanalysis ([arXiv:2302.06530](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.06530), Shamir) argues the residual
post-mirror asymmetry is real and agrees with other methods. **§1 already scopes Shamir out of the
claim boundary — keep that.** Record the split as context for why the question is contested, not as a
second target.
